title: Echo and Colony
premise: Wren Sandoval, a terraformer and cargo hauler in the contested orbits of Kepler Station, discovers the colony's children are all dreaming the same dream — a message from the long-silent first colony, Meridian, believed destroyed in the war's opening strike. The dream is actually a compressed distress archive: proof the war began on a lie engineered by the Colonial Authority to seize Meridian's terraforming patents. Hunted by Authority enforcers and distrusted by rebel factions who want the message weaponized, Wren must smuggle the children's decoded testimony to the neutral relay at Thessaly Gate before the Authority can purge the archive — and before the rebels can twist it into a justification for retaliation. In the end, Wren broadcasts the raw truth unedited to both fleets, ending the war not with victory but with shared grief, and chooses to stay and rebuild Meridian's garden rather than return to the life they knew.
about_author: C. M. Vasquez is the pen name of a former agricultural engineer who spent six years designing closed-loop habitats before turning to fiction full-time. Their stories explore what justice looks like when the law itself is the crime, and they write from a converted greenhouse office.

chapters.title: The Garden for the Unborn
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Establishes Wren's decade tending Kepler Station's seed vault and hauling cargo through contested orbits. The emotional beat is quiet devotion — a life built for a future that keeps receding — ending with Wren witnessing a child wake screaming from a dream she describes in perfect technical detail.

chapters.title: Shared Sleep
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. More children report the identical dream: a green valley, a voice counting down. Wren's old friend Dr. Imani Reyes confirms the dreams contain structured data. The beat is unease deepening into dread as Wren realizes the dream's imagery matches Meridian — the colony everyone says is dead.

chapters.title: What the Authority Buried
chapters.summary: Imani's POV. Decoding begins; the dream-data carries Meridian's authentication codes, which should be impossible. An Authority audit team arrives unannounced. The beat is paranoia — Imani hides the decoder as enforcers walk the corridors, and we learn the war's first strike has no independent record.

chapters.title: Cargo Run to Nowhere
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren takes a routine haul that's actually an Authority trap to flush out the dream-leak; a sympathetic dock officer tips them off. The beat is betrayal and quick thinking as Wren jettisons the trap manifest and realizes someone inside the Authority is helping them.

chapters.title: The Children's Testimony
chapters.summary: Dual POV, Wren and twelve-year-old Odile Voss, the strongest dreamer. The children describe the countdown's endpoint: a date six weeks out. The beat is tenderness and terror — Odile asks Wren if the voice in the dream is her grandmother, listed dead at Meridian.

chapters.title: Rebels at the Airlock
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The Free Orbit faction, led by the charismatic Cass Merah, offers protection in exchange for the archive — intending to broadcast a doctored version blaming Authority leadership alone. The beat is the first hard choice: Wren refuses, and makes an enemy of an ally.

chapters.title: Interrogation Light
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, captive. Authority interrogator Deputy Director Hale probes Wren with unsettling courtesy, revealing the Authority has known about the dreams for months and has been editing what the children receive. The beat is psychological pressure — Hale offers Wren the truth in fragments, each one a hook.

chapters.title: The Man in the Walls
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The children, communicating through their shared dream, guide Odile to the station's sealed maintenance levels where a hidden transmitter has been feeding the Authority's false dream-version. The beat is childhood courage — Odile sabotages it and meets the mystery ally: a disgraced Authority archivist, Sen Okafor.

chapters.title: Okafor's Confession
chapters.summary: Sen Okafor's POV. He reveals the war began when Authority command destroyed their own relay and blamed Meridian to seize terraforming patents; the children's dreams are Meridian's last broadcast, finally reaching minds young enough to receive raw data. The beat is grief and guilt — he helped build the lie.

chapters.title: Fracture
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren escapes custody with Okafor's help but learns Imani has handed partial data to Cass Merah to protect the children. The beat is heartbreak — loyalty and truth pull in opposite directions, and Wren must choose which friend to trust with the ending.

chapters.title: The Countdown Is Real
chapters.summary: Imani's POV. The decoded archive isn't just testimony: it's a dead-man's switch. If Meridian's surviving sleepers aren't acknowledged by the countdown's end, their life-support fails. The beat is escalation — this is no longer history to expose but lives to save, and every faction wants the switch for leverage.

chapters.title: Thessaly Gate
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The run to the neutral relay through mined corridors, with the children aboard as living decoders. The beat is breathless momentum — Wren's hauler, the Long Acre, threaded through wreckage of the first battle, Odile navigating by dream.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Wreckfield
chapters.summary: Dual POV, Wren and Cass Merah. Cass's rebels attack to seize the archive mid-flight; Wren outmaneuvers them but takes crippling damage, and Cass sees the children's faces and wavers. The beat is moral rupture — Cass realizes what her cause has become, and lets them go.

chapters.title: What Odile Saw
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. In the dream, the voice finally answers Odile directly: her grandmother is alive, and Meridian has been hiding for ten years, afraid that surfacing means war. The beat is wonder and weight — a child carrying a message that could end or ignite everything, and knowing it.

chapters.title: Hale's Offer
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Hale intercepts the Long Acre and offers a deal: deliver the archive to the Authority, and Meridian's sleepers live under Authority 'protection' — and the lie stays buried. The beat is seduction of the reasonable villain; Hale genuinely believes peace requires the lie.

chapters.title: The Long Acre's Last Burn
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren fakes compliance, then burns hard for Thessaly Gate with Hale's ship in pursuit; Okafor sacrifices his escape pod as a decoy and is captured. The beat is sacrifice — Wren arrives at the relay with minutes left and a broken ship, carrying everyone's hopes and debts.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Wren and Odile, dual POV, at the climax. At the relay, Wren must choose: Cass's edited version, Hale's sanitized version, or the raw archive — including Meridian's own failures that started the patent war. Wren broadcasts it all, unedited, to both fleets. The beat is terrifying clarity: truth offered whole, with no guarantee.

chapters.title: The Silence After
chapters.summary: Imani's POV. Both fleets go quiet; the countdown stops as Meridian's sleepers are acknowledged. But Authority hardliners move to seize the relay, and Hale — shaken by the raw archive — must decide whose side she's on. The beat is held breath, the war balanced on one woman's conscience.

chapters.title: Hale's Choice
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. Hale arrests her own hardliner commanders, using her authority to freeze the seizure, and publicly confirms the archive's authenticity. The beat is redemption without absolution — she ends the war she helped sustain, knowing she'll be tried for it, and accepts that.

chapters.title: Meridian Rising
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The first shuttle from Meridian docks at Thessaly Gate; Odile meets the grandmother from her dreams. Justice outside the law has worked, barely, and now the slow legal reckoning begins. The beat is release — grief and joy in the same breath, ten years of war ending in an embrace.

chapters.title: Seeds for a Shared Sky
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Weeks later: trials underway, Cass rebuilding the Free Orbits into a civilian federation, Okafor testifying from custody. Wren is offered honors and refuses them. The beat is quiet reckoning — identity rebuilt around truth rather than loyalty to any flag, and the cost honestly counted.

chapters.title: The Garden for the Living
chapters.summary: Wren and Odile, closing dual POV. Wren replants the seed vault's first bed at Meridian itself — the garden finally meant for people who exist. Odile dreams, for the first time, of nothing at all. The final beat is peace earned, not given: a future that arrived, and people ready to tend it.
